newsitem.title: SPAIN: Acerinox set to improve in 1997 - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Acerinox set to improve in 1997 - analysts.

text.p: A fall in nine-month earnings at Spanish stainless steel producer Acerinox was largely in line with expectations and the company should rebound towards the end of the year and into 1997, analysts said on Thursday.

"Although the figures look poor and we have to go back to 1993 to see such bad figures, the results compare very well with its most direct competitor Avesta Sheffield," said Jaime Vazquez, analyst at Salomon Brothers in London.
"It's very impressive given Avesta made a loss of 4 billion pesetas in the third quarter, while Acerinox made a profit of 2.5 billion," he added.
Acerinox said on Thursday its consolidated net profit fell 54.74 percent to 11.93 billion pesetas for the first nine months of 1996. Net profits for the first half of 1996 were 9.43 billion pesetas.
Four analysts forecast on average that the company's net profit would fall to 12.29 billion pesetas for the first nine months of 1996 from 26.35 billion pesetas in the corresponding period of 1995.
Analysts said they expected an improvement in prices and demand to begin to be reflected in fourth quarter earnings.

Acerinox raised its prices five percent from September 1 citing the strength of its order book, after prices slumped earlier in the year. It added on Thursday that the market had fully accepted the increases.
But analysts said they did not expect increases to impact until the very end of the year.

"Although the basic price was increased in September, the alloy surcharge was lower during the period, and prices remained unchanged," said one analyst. Stainless steel prices comprise two elements, he added, the basic price and the alloy surcharge which depends on the evolution of nickel prices.

On the demand side, some analysts said they thought final demand had remained largely flat although it was hard to tell without a breakdown of the results which would not be given until the end of the year.
The company said in August it expected international demand for stainless steel to recover from September. On Thursday it said production had reached record levels at its plants.
But some analysts said this strength was largely due to the fact that the destocking process was now over.
Analysts warned that end of year results could be distorted by two items, which the company has not yet revealed.

"We are expecting two adjustments before year end. Firstly the contribution from Mexinox and an extraordinary item to reflect the insurance claim from the fire," said Jaime Vazquez, analyst at Salomon Brothers in London.
Analysts said this year's contributions from its 33 percent holding in Mexican steel company Mexinox had not yet been published and this could be a source for adjustment at year end.
In addition, an insurance claim after a fire damaged cables at one of the company's five cold-rolled presses at its Campo de Gibraltar factory in July, could affect the results, they added.
The company has not specified the extent of the claim and analysts said it could appear as an extraordinary item.
Most analysts said they expected the group to bounce back next year with a recovery in the stainless steel market, although some said the bounce would be more subdued than others.
"We see profits more than doubling in 1997 to 32 billion pesetas, compared with our forecast of 15.9 billion pesetas for 1996," said Salomon's Vazquez.
The company warned in June that it would not reach last year's record profit level in 1996. In 1995 the group clocked a 200 percent increase in net profits to 34.39 billion pesetas.
Acerinox's shares were trading down 1.14 percent at 15,660 by 1500 GMT. But most analysts said they expected the price to improve given the outlook for the company was improving.
